prompt: Write the body (about 120 words) of a letter of representation from a personal injury lawyer to an auto insurer. The client was hurt in a low-speed head-on collision. Ask that all contact go through the law firm, ask for the policy limits, and ask the insurer to keep all evidence. No salutation, no signature, no names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1483; do not mention it.)
text:
This firm represents the injured party in connection with the motor vehicle collision involving your insured. Please direct all further communication regarding this matter to our office and do not contact our client directly. Our client sustained injuries in a low-speed head-on collision, and we are gathering information to evaluate the full extent of the claim.

We request that you disclose the bodily injury liability limits of the policy under which your insured is covered, along with any other policies that may apply to this loss, including excess or umbrella coverage. Please also provide the name of the adjuster assigned to this claim and the claim number.

We further demand that your company preserve all evidence relating to this collision. This includes the claim file, photographs, vehicle data and event data recorder information, repair or total loss records, recorded statements, telematics data, and any communications with your insured or third parties. Failure to preserve this evidence may result in sanctions and adverse inferences in any subsequent litigation.

We look forward to your prompt written response confirming receipt of this letter and your compliance with these requests.
